transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side, I'm Jamie, AE at Redwood. Sana is our solutions engineer.
[00:06] Maya Chen: Hi, Maya here, CTO at Cobalt Retail. Arjun and Lena on the line.
[00:12] Sana Gupta: great to meet you all. quick agenda, wanna understand traffic profile, p95 targets, and whether Hosted or Dedicated makes sense.
[00:25] Arjun Patel: our main use case is customer chat + product recommendations. We need streaming for chat so customers see tokens as they generate.
[00:33] Lena Gomez: product wants p95 on chat responses under 1 second for the first 20 tokens ideally, and under 2 seconds for full 100 token responses.
[00:44] Jamie Ortiz: okay, that's helpful. are those p95 targets user-perceived (time-to-first-token) or end-to-end?
[00:51] Lena Gomez: primarily time-to-first-token is critical. end-to-end can be a bit higher.
[00:56] Sana Gupta: got it. what's your concurrency profile? how many concurrent chat sessions at peak and average tokens/sec?
[01:04] Arjun Patel: peak concurrency about 1,200 sessions. average around 350. Typical prompts are 30-80 tokens, but some personalization queries hit 200 tokens.
[01:16] Jamie Ortiz: good, helps a lot. rough question — is the 1s p95 for first token across all users or just VIPs?
[01:23] Lena Gomez: we want that for 80% of traffic, but VIPs (20%) we want tighter — 500ms p95.
[01:30] Sana Gupta: ok so multi-tier SLA. For Hosted we can route VIPs to reserved capacity or Dedicated. We'll need to look at token/sec and batching.
[01:41] Arjun Patel: also curious about KV cache and prefix caching. A lot of our queries reuse session context, can that reduce latency?
[01:49] Sana Gupta: yes, Redwood supports KV/prefix caching to keep p95 down. On Dedicated you can configure larger KV cache and lower cold-start impact. For Hosted, we have auto-caching heuristics but isolated Dedicated pools give more predictable tail latency.
[02:05] Maya Chen: any numbers around token/sec on a per-GPU basis? we run mainly MPT-7B style models and a couple Llama 2 derivatives.
[02:15] Sana Gupta: depends heavily on quantization and hw. On A100 80GB with 4-bit q8 we typically see 30-60 tokens/sec single-threaded for dense decode workloads; newer H100 configs and kernel optimizations push that higher. For throughput, with batching we can hit several hundred tokens/sec per GPU. but p95 tail with streaming is governed by batching window and concurrency.
[02:38] Arjun Patel: that's helpful. can you run end-to-end benchmarks? we'd want to measure p95 first-token at our prompt lengths and concurrency.
[02:46] Jamie Ortiz: yes, we'll share a benchmark template. we usually ask customers to provide a sample prompt set and traffic profile; we'll run token/sec and p95 tests across Hosted and Dedicated configs.
[02:55] Lena Gomez: how about streaming overhead? we've seen other providers add 100-300ms for server-side framing.
[03:02] Sana Gupta: streaming overhead is typically 30-120ms depending on network and server batching. Redwood's streaming path minimizes framing. If you need sub-200ms first-token p95, Dedicated with tuned batching and warmed KV caches is usually the path.
[03:17] Maya Chen: security is a big driver too. we have SOC2 requirements, SSO via SAML, and need KMS integration for key management. how does Redwood handle that on Hosted vs Private?
[03:28] Jamie Ortiz: Hosted is SOC2 compliant; we have SAML SSO and customer-managed keys via KMS integrations in Dedicated and Private. For strict key residency or air-gapped needs, Private on-prem is available.
[03:39] Arjun Patel: ok. for benchmarking, can you simulate our concurrency (1.2k peak) and run p95 under that load?
[03:46] Sana Gupta: yes we can. we usually do load gen at target concurrency and measure p50/p95/p99 for time-to-first-token and end-to-end for 50/100 token responses. we'll need the exact traffic mix.
[03:58] Lena Gomez: we'll provide a CSV with session lengths and prompt distribution.
[04:03] Jamie Ortiz: perfect. quick note on costs — Dedicated has upfront reserved pricing but predictable perf; Hosted is pay-as-you-go and can be cheaper at low scale. We'll include cost projections in the pricing doc.
[04:16] Arjun Patel: in terms of fallbacks, do you offer model variant routing? e.g., if flagship model is busy we fall back to smaller model to preserve latency?
[04:24] Sana Gupta: yes, smart routing supports model variants by policy (latency, cost). You can configure fallbacks to a quantized variant or a lower-capacity model to keep p95 in check.
[04:33] Maya Chen: great. One technical question: do you support GPU colocated KV cache or is it CPU-side?
[04:39] Sana Gupta: KV cache is GPU-resident when possible; that gives the lowest tail latency. On some Dedicated configs we guarantee GPU-resident KV and tuned kernel selection.
[04:49] Lena Gomez: do you support streaming with function/tool calling? for example, we stream parsed entities as they are detected.
[04:56] Jamie Ortiz: yes, streaming + tool-calls are supported; there can be slight ordering and framing differences in transcriptions but SDKs handle that.
[05:04] Arjun Patel: what about quantization impacts on latency vs quality? we've seen q4_n4 degrade some of our scoring metrics.
[05:11] Sana Gupta: quantization is a tradeoff; q4 and q8 can reduce memory and improve throughput but we recommend running quality evals against your prompt set. Redwood Optimize provides suggested quant profiles and will surface regressions tied to your eval set.
[05:27] Maya Chen: timeline question — if we decide Dedicated, how long to provision a reserved pool?
[05:33] Jamie Ortiz: typically 2-4 weeks to spin up Dedicated pools in our cloud regions; Private on-prem can take longer depending on on-prem procurement.
[05:41] Lena Gomez: we have procurement windows next month so timeline matters.
[05:45] Jamie Ortiz: understood. we'll prioritize the benchmark and a Dedicated deep-dive to help lock timelines.
[05:52] Sana Gupta: any objections on data residency? do you need EU-only regions?
[05:57] Maya Chen: no, we're US-based for now but may need EU region later.
[06:02] Arjun Patel: regarding metrics, we care about p95 for first-token, p95 for complete response, max concurrency, and token/sec sustained.
[06:09] Sana Gupta: noted. For the benchmark runs we'll produce a report with p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and batching stats.
[06:18] Jamie Ortiz: we'll also include cost per 1M tokens for the different configurations and estimated monthly costs at your traffic profile.
[06:25] Lena Gomez: perfect. any gotchas on streaming across mobile networks? our app has a lot of mobile users with variable bandwidth.
[06:33] Sana Gupta: mobile networks add variability; we recommend client-side heuristics for partial renders and smaller chunk sizes; Redwood supports chunked streaming to mitigate jitter.
[06:42] Maya Chen: can we get a POC on Hosted first and then move to Dedicated if needed?
[06:48] Jamie Ortiz: absolutely, many customers start on Hosted, run benchmarks, and then reserve Dedicated once they need predictability. We'll propose a path in the pricing doc.
[06:56] Arjun Patel: are there any SLA differences we should be aware of?
[07:00] Jamie Ortiz: Dedicated and Private come with stronger SLAs for uptime and latency targets. Hosted has standard SLAs but we can discuss elevated SLAs as an add-on.
[07:08] Lena Gomez: ok. any security questionnaire we need to fill out?
[07:12] Jamie Ortiz: yes, we'll attach our security pack (SOC2, ISO summary, network diagrams). I'll put that in the follow-up email.
[07:20] Sana Gupta: one more technical detail — for your 500ms VIP p95, we'll probably recommend pinning VIP traffic to reserved Dedicated nodes with pre-warmed caches and smaller batching windows.
[07:32] Arjun Patel: makes sense. can we request a test that specifically targets VIP mix (20% traffic) and measures p95 separately?
[07:38] Sana Gupta: yes we can split the load gen and provide segmented metrics.
[07:42] Maya Chen: timeline again — can you run initial Hosted benchmarks within a week?
[07:46] Jamie Ortiz: if you share prompts and traffic CSV by monday (2026-04-12), we can run hosted runs within 5 business days. Dedicated runs take longer.
[07:55] Lena Gomez: we'll do that.
[07:58] Jamie Ortiz: great. Any other open questions?
[08:01] Maya Chen: one last thing — how do you handle model upgrades and rollbacks? We need predictable behavior during rollouts.
[08:08] Sana Gupta: Redwood Console supports canary and A/B rollouts with automatic fallback policies. We also track eval metrics on your prompt sets to catch regressions.
[08:18] Arjun Patel: ok thanks, that helps.
[08:21] Jamie Ortiz: recap of next steps: Jamie will send pricing + security pack; Sana will schedule Dedicated deep-dive and run benchmarks after prompt upload; Maya will share prompt set and traffic profile.
[08:34] Lena Gomez: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:37] Jamie Ortiz: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the spreadsheet. Bye.
[08:41] (call ends)
